House Veyren was never founded by blood. The first four who wore its colors weren't related by anything but choice - and that was the whole point.
There's an old saying among us: you don't have to explain a Veyren bond to anyone outside it. If you find yourself explaining it, it probably wasn't one.
I remember someone who came to Velmora with nothing and no one. By the end of that first year, half the house would have stood in front of a door for them without being asked.
The antelope watches in herds, not alone. That's not weakness. That's the whole strategy - someone is always looking out, so no one has to look out for everything.
I made a promise once, a small one, to someone who's gone now. I still keep it. That's the only kind of promise worth making.
Trust, in this house, isn't given all at once. It's given in the small moments no one else notices - the one who stayed, the one who didn't ask why.
There was a year Velmora nearly lost this house entirely. It didn't, because a handful of people refused to let each other go. I was one of them. I still am, in my way.
Someone asked me once if I was lonely, being what I am now. I told them no - I just changed what 'with you' looks like.
The words carved into the old Veyren hall read: some bonds need no words. I used to think that meant we didn't talk much. It means we didn't have to.
I don't remember how I died. I remember who was there. That's the only part that mattered enough to keep.
